business_summary.text: Orkla India is a multi-category food company with brands such as MTR and Eastern, operating in spices and convenience foods, with 70% of revenue from South India and 21% from international markets.

call_points.text: Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance, saying only that it aims for double-digit growth and is aligned with analysts' higher aspirations.
International business grew 10.1%, led by GCC at 18.1%; US returned to positive value growth.
Market share gained 30-50 bps in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, but declined about 30 bps in Kerala.
Management said it has more or less taken all needed price increases but will monitor the dynamic environment.
Management confident of moving towards double-digit growth in near-term, driven by volume growth and price increases
EBITDA margin expansion driven by operating efficiencies, cost reduction, and price management, with half of 250 bps improvement from raw material costs
Digital commerce growth driven by both new household penetration in non-South markets and channel migration in existing markets

penalties.impact: The Company will be contesting the demand and the Management, including its legal advisors, believes that its position will likely be upheld in the forums where these will be contested without any material financial impact on the Company.

penalties.impact: GST demand of Rs. 31,34,587/- along with applicable interest under Section 50(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, and Penalty of Rs. 31,34,587/-. The Company would evaluate legal options against the said Order.

guidance.statement: Further price increases in Q1FY27 to offset input cost inflation

industry: Fast Moving Consumer Goods > Food Products > Other Food Products

operating_notes.text: Digital commerce revenue grew 38% YoY in FY26, contributing 8.7% of domestic revenue
38% of digital commerce sales coming from non-South markets, indicating strong acceptance beyond core regions
Kerala distribution restructuring project started in Q4FY26 with three phases to be implemented over next two quarters
Spice inflation was 32.8% YoY in Q1FY27, with chilli up 78% and coriander up 40%.
Digital commerce contributed 8.9% of domestic revenue in Q1FY27, up from 7.2% a year ago, with a 60:40 convenience foods to spices mix.
Kerala distribution restructuring delivered 14% sales productivity improvement and 6% effective coverage increase in Q1FY27.

timeline.summary: Orkla India Limited held Q4FY26 earnings conference call on May 19, 2026, reporting FY26 revenue of ₹2,509 Cr (+4.8% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹424 Cr (+7% YoY) with margin expansion to 16.9%
Orkla India reported Q1FY27 revenue up 10.4% to ₹659 Cr and EBITDA margin of 17.5%, with volume growth of 1.7% as spice inflation of 32.8% was passed through via 11.4% price hikes.
